claim: A four-task cycle (describe problem, generate causes, test, repair and evaluate) with loop-backs describes real human troubleshooting; it is recursive, not linear.
agent_test: Compare a strict linear S1-S4 against a looped version with back-edges on one fault set at equal tokens.
audit: downgraded 2026-10-31 by check_established.py: only 1 opened source(s) from distinct authors

claim: Teaching a general diagnostic method plus a system breakdown beat content-only training in the field (about 2x faults fixed, less time), but the only primary source is one abstract with no effect size. Gap search: the full text was still not reachable (Pure, TNO, Crossref carry the abstract only), so no N or effect size exists in our notes.
agent_test: Ablate a method scaffold against added domain notes at equal tokens.

claim: Split-half search needs a system model and a stated prediction first; without a model humans cannot predict and fall back to exhaustive replacement.
agent_test: Give the agent a component graph; compare split-half chosen by code against free-form probe choice.
audit: downgraded 2026-10-31 by check_established.py: only 1 opened source(s) from distinct authors

claim: Recall of a past fault is fast but causes needless repairs: 5 of 8 student pairs made wrong or needless changes. No LLM study measures needless repairs after recall; indirect support only: LLMs commit early and rely on that answer (39% average multi-turn drop) and follow planted bias cues (10-26% accuracy loss).
agent_test: Require a refuting test before any repair; count needless actions.

claim: A separate evaluate-after-repair check is needed and the agent must be allowed to conclude 'no fault': on healthy networks agents report a fault in 11-24% of answered runs (FaulT-Bench, standard ticket; up to 74% for one agent with a vague ticket), and 3 of 4 agents did so on AIOpsLab's 2 no-fault problems. The fix itself (a no-fault exit plus verify gate) has not been tested by anyone.
agent_test: Add healthy-system and no-fault items; measure false-alarm rate with and without a verify gate.

claim: ReAct-style evidence loops lower hallucination but do not reliably raise root-cause accuracy over simple baselines: Roy et al. 35 vs 39 percent (hallucination 4 vs 12 vs 40 percent); SIA benchmark ReAct 69.0 vs direct prompting 67.3 and 67.5 with overlapping 95% intervals. SADE reports ReAct far below a structured agent (0.44 vs 0.77 F1), so the result depends on the comparison.
agent_test: Replicate ReAct vs CoT on one incident set and count unsupported claims.

claim: Most ReAct failures on root-cause analysis are insufficient evidence (66 percent of wrong predictions), so the scaffold needs a 'get more evidence' exit instead of forcing a verdict.
agent_test: Allow an abstain-and-probe action; measure whether forced verdicts drop.

claim: Generating a wide candidate set matters more than selecting among candidates: removing hypothesis expansion cut potential from 89.2 to 79.3; ToT shows a 22.5 point gap between potential and final.
agent_test: Vary candidate breadth at equal tokens; separate presence of the true cause from selection accuracy.

claim: Choosing the next question by expected information gain over a candidate fault set raises success (GPT-4 43.7 to 67.3 percent on troubleshooting dialogues) and beats CoT-SC and Reflexion; discriminating follow-up questions also help in SIA ablation (79.2 vs 75.0). Closest LLM-versus-code test: in BED-LLM (20 Questions, 6 LLMs) code-computed expected information gain beat the LLM picking among the same candidate questions (example GPT-4o Animals 93 vs 70 percent; column labels inferred) and beat equal-split (83). QuestBench: models reach only 40-50 percent on picking the right clarifying question in Logic-Q and Planning-Q.
agent_test: Code-computed information-gain probe choice vs LLM-chosen probe.

claim: Structured, phase-gated or SOP-guided diagnosis beats plain ReAct in LLM root-cause tasks (SADE F1 0.77 vs 0.44 in text, 0.40 in Fig. 1; same-backbone baseline 0.55, so +21.5 points from the policy; Flow-of-Action 64.0 vs 35.5 percent; SIA 79.2 vs ReAct 69.0 with overlapping intervals). Not at equal tokens: SADE median input 344k vs 55k for ReAct and 189k for the same-backbone baseline. All gains come from authors' own harnesses and LLM judges.
agent_test: Phase-gated scaffold vs free ReAct at matched token budget.

claim: Observation quality limits diagnosis: removing traces cut GPT-4o diagnosis pass@1 from 13.81 (or 18.10, paper inconsistent) to 9.52; diagnosis falls with chain length from 36 percent to 5 percent.
agent_test: Mask observation sources and log which probes the agent picks.

claim: Intrinsic self-correction without an external signal does not help and can hurt (GPT-4 GSM8K 95.5 to 89.0); gains appear only with an oracle or external feedback. Kamoi et al. survey: no fair demonstration of gain from prompted self-feedback except tasks where checking is much easier than generating.
agent_test: Verify with an external test, not self-critique; include a self-critique-only arm.

claim: Forced reflection as debiasing is conditional and unproven for always-on use. Humans: a feedback-based immunisation exercise (not in-the-moment reflection) helped residents only on bias-exposed vignettes (0.40 vs 0.24, N=91); guided reflection did nothing for final diagnoses in students (strict accuracy 0.47/0.42/0.41, N=186) and flipped correct answers to wrong ones as often as the reverse (62 percent backfires in the short condition). LLMs: a differential-diagnosis prompt cut GPT-3.5 accuracy by 8 points; always-asking hurt (-11.3 percent) while confidence-gated asking helped (+22.3 percent) in MediQ.
agent_test: Trigger structured reflection only on a signal (surprise or impasse); compare with always-on.

claim: Diagnostic-style prompts give no reliable gain for a strong LLM on multiple-choice diagnosis (GPT-4 72-78 percent, none significant).
agent_test: Check whether style prompts matter on fault-diagnosis items.

claim: Step budget effects are agent-specific: GPT-3.5 plateaued beyond 5 steps while ReAct and FLASH kept improving to 20; operations feedback is weak compared with code tests.
agent_test: Sweep step budget per scaffold arm.

claim: Experts use fast rule-based recall first and slow model-based reasoning only when rules fail (Rasmussen); this supports a recall-first, search-on-impasse policy. Seen only through secondary summaries.
agent_test: Memory-hit-first vs always-search policy.

claim: Retrieval of past cases helps LLM root-cause analysis only modestly; lexical-metric changes were tiny or negative, and generic output is a failure mode. RCACopilot shows why: 24.96 percent of incidents (163 of 653) had a new root-cause category, so a case library cannot cover them. No study tested case libraries with human judges.
agent_test: Case-library retrieval vs none at equal tokens, human-judged.

claim: Multi-agent LLM failures are dominated by step repetition (15.7 percent), missing completion recognition (12.4) and proceeding on wrong assumptions (6.8); AIOpsLab shows repeated-call and apologise-retry loops.
agent_test: Loop detector and completion-check ablation.

claim: Forcing an early cause is unnecessary: some human solvers keep observing until a cause emerges.
agent_test: Allow extended observation before S2 and compare.

claim: Over-diagnosis of healthy systems depends on whether the report gives something checkable: with the same 72 healthy networks, over-diagnosis was 17 percent for a standard ticket, 31 for a vague novice ticket, 47 for a ticket with no identifiers, and confident wrong tickets were refuted more easily than vague ones.
agent_test: Test a rule that routes 'nothing checkable' to 'gather a checkable fact' vs picking a benign anomaly.

claim: Structure helps localisation but not the no-fault exit: the phase-gated SADE agent had the highest false-alarm rate on healthy networks (24 percent vs 16 ReAct and 11 Claude-Code baseline) while being best-grounded in its reasoning (0.933 vs 0.845). Authors of FaulT-Bench and SADE overlap.
agent_test: Add an explicit stopping criterion for 'no fault' and measure false alarms with and without it on the same clean systems.

claim: Probe choice should be computed, not asked: with identical candidate questions, code-computed expected information gain beat LLM judgement of the most informative question by a wide margin in 20 Questions (inferred example 93 vs 70 percent; mean gain over prompt-only +37.4 points). Not yet tested on fault graphs.
agent_test: On a component graph, compare code-computed split-half or EIG against LLM-chosen probes at equal call count.

claim: An ask-or-answer gate keyed to confidence beats always-on questioning: asking follow-up questions by plain prompt lowered diagnostic accuracy by 11.3 percent, and abstention based on rationale plus self-consistency gave +22.3 percent, leaving a 10.3 percent gap to full information.
agent_test: Gate probing and reflection on a stated insufficiency signal; compare with always-on.

claim: Jonassen and Hung 2006 is an untested design proposal (conceptual model, hypothesis-testing simulator, case library with case-based reasoning); in the accessible text it reports no participants or effect sizes, and no test of the case-library design was found.
agent_test: Treat 'ask what an expert did' as a hypothesis; test it before relying on it.

claim: Expert orientation effect in circuit troubleshooting is small: higher-expertise people spend relatively more time orienting and fixate more on a fault-related component. The abstract gives no numbers.
agent_test: Give S1 explicit time and a fixed check of the fault-related part before hypotheses.

claim: Scoring that credits a case when the right cause appears anywhere in a list of alternatives makes reflection look helpful (0.47 to 0.70-0.72, eta-squared 0.18) while strict final-diagnosis accuracy does not move (0.47 to 0.41-0.42).
agent_test: Score only the final selected cause; report potential and final separately, as SIA does.

claim: LLMs commit early under piece-by-piece information and then rely on that answer: 39 percent average drop in multi-turn vs single-turn (aptitude -15 percent, unreliability +112 percent) across 15 LLMs. Partial, indirect evidence for the recall-first risk.
agent_test: Forbid a repair before a refuting probe; count needless actions.

claim: The 2026 gains (SADE, SIA, FaulT-Bench) are not independently reproduced: SADE and FaulT-Bench share authors and judge (gpt-5-mini); SIA uses its own LLM rubric and LLM user simulator; SIA's margin over ReAct has overlapping 95% intervals. SIA holds on two other backbones (+6.2, +7.7) inside the same paper.
agent_test: Re-run with a different judge family and a human-checked sample before trusting the sizes.

claim: Matched-token comparisons are missing: SADE used a median 344k input tokens vs 55k for ReAct and 189k for the same-backbone baseline; SIA asks about twice the questions of ReAct; a fair-baseline study found tool-using prompting often no better than no-tool baselines at orders-of-magnitude more tokens.
agent_test: Run cycle vs ReAct vs direct prompt with a fixed token cap per arm on one fault set.
